items.title: Lillian Hardin Armstrong Interview, 1959-07-01
items.q: No, Louis was working with me that time. It wasn't Ollie Powers. I had the band there for a short time.

ctx.x: Yeah, on the west side. But I didn't work with him any place else. So when Louis was working at the Dreamland with Ollie Powers Band, that's after he'd left Oliver, everybody started talking about Louis playing because it was the first time he'd been able to be heard alone, you see. So Freddie heard about people talking about Louis one night. No, Louis was working with me that time. It wasn't Ollie Powers. I had the band there for a short time. items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-16
items.q: When I went into Chicago I was sitting with Joe, Johnny Dots, Baby Dots and all of them good. Leo on piano and Joe Arroyo and Lauren at Horn.

ctx.x: working with men that are better than you and I guess there was a time when there was someone better than you when you were awfully young.

All of my life in music and whatever happened to me right today comes from observing some of the musicians that were playing something. And I was always lucky to play with good musicians. When I went into Chicago I was sitting with Joe, Johnny Dots, Baby Dots and all of them good. Leo on piano and Joe Arroyo and Lauren at Horn. I said, why didn't we do it? Now, I went into the front set with Carol Dickerson's orchestra which was owned by Joe Glazer, my manager, and Joe Glazer and Joe Rollins who was called the…
I wouldn't listen to it. I've noticed you've talked a lot about Joe Oliver, and he must have been a tremendous influence.
